types.name: Aaron
types.description: Aaron, brother of Moses and first high priest of Israel.

types.name: Abel
types.description: Abel, the just son of Adam whose innocent blood was shed by his brother Cain.

types.name: Adam
types.description: Adam, the first man, whose creation and fall prefigure Christ as the New Adam.

types.name: Ahithophel
types.description: Achitophel, David's trusted counselor who betrayed him; a figure of the perfidious Judas (Ps 40:10, 'lifted up his heel').

types.name: Anointing of Kings, Priests, and Prophets
types.displayName: Anointing of Kings, Priests, and Prophets

types.name: Antiochus Epiphanes
types.description: The Hellenistic king and great persecutor of God's people (the 'little horn'); a figure of Antichrist.

types.name: Babylon
types.description: The ancient city of Babylon, the city of confusion, idolatry, and oppression of God's people.

types.name: Babylon the Great (the Harlot)
types.description: The mystical Babylon of Revelation — Rome and all wicked great cities / the multitude of the wicked who persecute the faithful — destined for judgment.

types.name: Balaam
types.description: Balaam, the pagan seer whose oracles included the prophecy of the Star from Jacob (Numbers 24:17).

types.name: Baptism
types.description: The sacrament of regeneration and incorporation into Christ through water and the Spirit.

types.name: Binding of Isaac
types.description: Abraham's willing sacrifice of his son Isaac on Mount Moriah (Genesis 22).

types.name: Brazen Serpent
types.description: The bronze serpent Moses lifted up on a pole in the wilderness so that all who looked upon it were healed (Numbers 21:8-9).

types.name: Burning Bush
types.description: The bush that burned with fire but was not consumed, in which the Angel of the Lord appeared to Moses (Exodus 3).

types.name: Ceremonial Law
types.description: The ceremonial and ritual prescriptions of the Old Testament Law, fulfilled and surpassed in the New Covenant.

types.name: Christ
types.description: Jesus Christ, the incarnate Son of God and fulfillment of all Old Testament types.

types.name: Christ the High Priest
types.description: Christ as the eternal high priest who offered himself once for all on the cross.

types.name: Christ's Ascension
types.description: Christ's ascension into heaven and exaltation to the right hand of the Father.

types.name: Christ's Passion
types.description: The suffering and crucifixion of Jesus Christ for the redemption of mankind.

types.name: Christ's Victory
types.description: Christ's triumph over sin, death, and Satan through the Paschal Mystery.

types.name: Circumcision
types.description: The sign of the covenant given to Abraham, marking incorporation into the people of God.

types.name: Cloud in the Desert
types.description: The pillar of cloud that guided and protected Israel through the wilderness.

types.name: Cyrus
types.description: Cyrus the Persian, who overthrew Babylon and freed the captives; a figure of the Messiah, the executor of divine justice (Isa 41:2; 45:1).

types.name: Daniel's Four Beasts (Four Empires)
types.description: The four beasts of Daniel 7 (lion/Chaldean, bear/Persian, leopard/Greek, and the fourth/Roman empire); the composite beast of Revelation alludes to them, figuring the final apostate empire of Antichrist.

types.name: Descent of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost
types.displayName: Descent of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost

types.name: Destruction of Jerusalem as Divine Judgment
types.displayName: Destruction of Jerusalem as Divine Judgment

types.name: Dietary Laws
types.description: The Mosaic laws distinguishing clean and unclean animals (Leviticus 11, Deuteronomy 14).

types.name: Divine Fire (Lightning)
types.description: The fire/lightning of God's power in Ps 28(29); a figure of the Holy Spirit appearing as tongues of fire at Pentecost.

types.name: Edom
types.description: Edom and Bosra, conquered enemies; taken mystically for the enemies of Christ and his Church.

types.name: Esau
types.description: Esau, who lost his birthright and privileges to Jacob; a figure of the reprobate, though not himself necessarily reprobate.

types.name: Esther
types.description: Queen Esther, who interceded for her people and secured their deliverance; a figure of the Church and of the Blessed Virgin Mary.

types.name: Eternal Life
types.description: The blessed inheritance of heaven promised to those who are baptized into Christ.

types.name: Eucharist
types.description: The sacrament of Christ's Body and Blood under the appearances of bread and wine.

types.name: Eve
types.description: Eve, the first woman and mother of all the living.

types.name: Feast of Pentecost
types.description: The Feast of Weeks (Shavuot), celebrating the firstfruits of the harvest and the giving of the Law at Sinai.

types.name: Final Judgment
types.description: The Last Judgment at the end of time, when Christ will judge the living and the dead.

types.name: Gideon
types.description: Gideon, judge of Israel who delivered his people with a small band chosen by God.

types.name: God's Deliverance from Sennacherib
types.description: God's overthrow of Sennacherib's army, terrifying the persecutors; a figure of the certainty of the final judgment.

types.name: God's Healing Word
types.description: God's word/command by which the sick were healed; read by the Fathers in the prophetical sense of Christ the Word who heals.

types.name: God's Wonders by Water
types.description: The many wonders God wrought by water in the Old Testament (Exodus plagues, provision in the wilderness); a figure of the grace conferred in baptism.

types.name: Gog and Magog
types.description: Gog and Magog of Ezekiel's prophecy — nations gathered against God's people; a figure of the last persecution of the Church under Antichrist before the final judgment.

types.name: Heaven
types.description: The heavenly tabernacle and city, the eternal dwelling place of God and his people (Apoc 15:5; Heb 12:22).

types.name: Heretics
types.description: Those who teach false doctrine and oppose the true faith within the Christian era.

types.name: Hezekiah
types.description: King Ezechias of Judah, righteous king delivered from the Assyrians; figure of Christ and of the Church persecuted yet increasing.

types.name: Holofernes
types.description: The pagan general in Judith who demands universal worship and divine status; a figure of Antichrist.

types.name: Holy Orders
types.description: The Sacrament of Holy Orders, by which men are ordained to the Christian priesthood.

types.name: Hosea
types.description: The prophet Osee, who took back the unfaithful woman; acting 'as a figure of the Lord, who has received an outrage' yet offers grace to penitent sinners.

types.name: Isaac
types.description: Isaac, son of the free-woman Sarah and child of promise; in Paul's allegory (Gal 4) a figure of the New Covenant, the free children of God, and the Church.

types.name: Isaiah (the prophet)
types.description: The prophet Isaiah, anointed by God's Spirit to preach good news to the poor; a figure of Christ the Anointed One (Luke 4:18).

types.name: Ishmael
types.description: Ishmael, son of Abraham by Hagar, the son of the bondwoman born according to the flesh.

types.name: Israel (Jeshurun)
types.description: Israel under the title Jeshurun, the beloved of God; a figure of the Messiah, the true Beloved.

types.name: Israel's Disobedience in the Wilderness
types.description: The murmurs, infidelities, and disobedience of the Hebrews in the desert; written 'in a figure' (1 Cor 10:6) as a warning that the sacraments without amendment bring condemnation.

types.name: Jacob
types.description: Jacob (Israel), patriarch whose life of struggle and sorrow prefigures Christ.

types.name: Jeremiah
types.description: The prophet Jeremiah, persecuted and afflicted; a figure of Christ in his sufferings.

types.name: Job
types.description: The innocent sufferer whose trials, vindication, and restoration figure Christ (the innocent man of sorrows), the Church, and the resurrection of the just.

types.name: John the Baptist
types.description: John the Baptist, who came in the spirit and power of Elijah to prepare the way before Christ's first coming (Matt 11:14; 17:11).

types.name: Jonah
types.description: The prophet Jonah, three days in the belly of the fish; a figure of Christ's resurrection (the sign of Jonas, Matt 12:40).

types.name: Crossing of the Jordan
types.description: Israel's passage through the Jordan River into the Promised Land under Joshua.

types.name: Josedec
types.description: Jesus son of Josedech, high priest who returned from exile and helped rebuild the temple (Hag, Zech); a figure of Christ the High Priest and builder of the spiritual temple.

types.name: Joseph
types.description: Joseph, son of Jacob, sold by his brothers yet exalted to deliver his people from famine.

types.name: Joshua
types.description: Joshua (Yehoshua), successor of Moses who led Israel into the Promised Land.

types.name: Judah
types.description: Judah, son of Jacob, from whose tribe the Messiah descends (Genesis 49).

types.name: Judas Maccabeus
types.description: The Maccabean warrior who conquered Idumea and fought to save his people; a glorious figure of Christ the victorious conqueror (read of the ascension).

types.name: Judith
types.description: The widow of Israel who delivered her people by slaying Holofernes; a figure of the Blessed Virgin Mary and of the Church.

types.name: Leah
types.description: Leah, first wife of Jacob, mother of six of the twelve tribes.

types.name: Leviathan
types.description: The great sea-monster of Job, fearsome yet subject to God; represents the devil under God's dominion.

types.name: Levitical Leprosy Laws
types.description: The Levitical laws governing the diagnosis, quarantine, and purification of leprosy (Leviticus 13-14).

types.name: Levitical Purifications (Ceremonial Washings)
types.description: The ceremonial purifications of the Old Law with water; figures of baptism and penance, in which the blood of Christ is applied to the soul.

types.name: Liver of the Fish (Tobit)
types.description: The fish's liver burned to expel the demon Asmodeus in Tobit; read mystically as the means of demonic deliverance.

types.name: Manna in the Desert
types.description: The bread from heaven that fed Israel during their forty years in the wilderness.

types.name: Mary
types.description: The Blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of God and Mother of the Church.

types.name: Melchizedek
types.description: The priest-king of Salem who offered bread and wine and blessed Abraham.

types.name: Miriam
types.description: Miriam, sister of Moses and Aaron, prophetess of Israel.

types.name: Moses
types.description: Moses, liberator and lawgiver of Israel, mediator of the Old Covenant.

types.name: Moses's Veil
types.description: The veil Moses placed over his face to hide the fading glory of the law (Exod 34); a figure of the obscurity and transience of the old covenant, removed in the unveiled glory of the new (2 Cor 3).

types.name: Nehemiah
types.description: Nehemiah, whose name means 'comforter of God,' sent by the king to rebuild Jerusalem; a figure of Christ sent to comfort and establish the Church.

types.name: Sacraments of the New Covenant
types.description: The seven sacraments instituted by Christ as signs and means of grace.

types.name: Noah
types.description: Noah, the just man who found favor with God and was preserved through the Flood.

types.name: Noah's Ark
types.description: The ark built by Noah that preserved his family through the flood waters.

types.name: Noah's Flood
types.description: The flood that cleansed the earth in the days of Noah, through which eight persons were saved by water.

types.name: Old Testament Priesthood
types.description: The Levitical priesthood established at Sinai for sacrifice and mediation.

types.name: Old Testament Sacrifices
types.description: The various sacrifices and offerings prescribed in the Law of Moses.

types.name: Passover
types.description: The feast commemorating Israel's liberation from Egypt, including the paschal lamb and unleavened bread.

types.name: Persecutors of the Church
types.description: Those who persecute the Christian Church and, like their OT figures, are ultimately judged.

types.name: Proselytes (Strangers in Israel)
types.description: Foreign strangers/proselytes who renounced idolatry, embraced Israel's religion, and were incorporated into the covenant community.

types.name: Raphael
types.description: The angel Raphael in Tobit, who appears in human form to guide and protect Tobias; commentary reads him as prefiguring Christ's assumption of human nature.

types.name: Rebecca
types.description: Rebecca, wife of Isaac, chosen by divine providence as bride for the patriarch's son.

types.name: Red Heifer
types.description: The red heifer sacrifice prescribed in Numbers 19, whose ashes mixed with water purified those defiled by contact with the dead.

types.name: Crossing of the Red Sea
types.description: Israel's passage through the Red Sea, liberated from Egyptian slavery and passing dry-shod through the waters.

types.name: Religious Orders (Consecrated Life)
types.description: The consecrated religious orders of the Church, professing poverty, chastity, and obedience in imitation of the apostles (Matt 19:12).

types.name: Return from Babylonian Captivity
types.description: The restored holy people returning from captivity to rebuilt Jerusalem, described by the prophets as a sanctified community; a figure of the Church.

types.name: Sanaballat
types.description: Sanballat, persecutor of the Jewish restoration and friend of Tobias; prefigures heretics who oppose the true faith.

types.name: Sarah
types.description: Sarah, wife of Abraham and mother of Isaac, the free woman whose son was born according to the promise.

types.name: Satan (the Devil)
types.description: The spiritual adversary who, despite his power, is ultimately subject to God and defeated by Christ.

types.name: Sennacherib
types.description: The Assyrian king who spoiled Samaria and Judah and despised God, then was brought to nothing; a figure of the persecutors of the Church.

types.name: Solomon
types.description: King Solomon, son of David, whose name means 'peaceable' and whose peaceful reign and temple-building prefigure Christ.

types.name: Spiritual Gifts of Christ
types.description: The grace and spiritual refreshment that flows from Christ to believers.

types.name: Temporal Chastisements of Israel
types.description: The temporal punishments inflicted on Israel for sin (e.g. the slaying of the murmurers, Num 25); types of eternal chastisement (1 Cor 10:11).

types.name: Temporal Rewards of the Old Law
types.description: The material blessings and temporal prosperity God granted the just under the Old Covenant, given as a figure of heavenly rewards.
types.displayName: Temporal Rewards of the Old Law

types.name: The Abomination of Desolation
types.description: The profanation of the temple foretold by Daniel (partly fulfilled by Pilate's and Adrian's images), prefiguring the abomination Antichrist will bring at the end.

types.name: The Adoration of the Magi
types.description: The wise men from the East who came to adore the infant Christ with gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh (Matt 2).

types.name: The Altar of Incense
types.description: The golden altar of incense in the holy place, where incense was offered morning and evening; signifies Christ the Mediator, through whose merits the prayers of the faithful ascend.

types.name: The Angel of the Lord
types.description: The angel who encamps round God's servants to guard them (Ps 33/34); read by the Fathers as figuring Christ the protector.

types.name: The Ark of the Covenant
types.description: The ark where God's presence dwelt, which David longed to be near; a figure of heaven, the place of God's presence.

types.name: The Ass and the Colt (Palm Sunday)
types.description: The ass and the colt of Zech 9:9, read by the Fathers as figuring the Jews (ass) and Gentiles (colt) to be loosed and brought to Christ, united in his Church.
types.displayName: The Ass and the Colt (Palm Sunday)

types.name: The Babylonian Exile
types.description: Israel's exile, deprived of religion, temple, and princes; a figure of the long desolation the Jews endured after rejecting Christ.

types.name: The Betrayal by Judas
types.description: Judas, who ate bread with Christ and was entrusted with the purse, betraying him with a kiss (John 13:18).

types.name: The Conversion of the Jews
types.description: The final conversion and restoration of the Jewish people, by which 'all Israel shall be saved' (Rom 11:26).

types.name: The Cup of Divine Wrath
types.description: The cup/chalice of God's judgment in which the dregs are reserved for sinners; a figure of the eschatological cup of wrath at the last judgment.

types.name: The Divine Chariot Theophany
types.description: God appearing on his chariot of winds/clouds (cf. Ezek 1:4) to come to David's aid; read by the Fathers as figuring Christ's ascension.

types.name: The Dove and the Olive Branch (Noah)
types.description: The dove returning to the ark with an olive branch (Gen 8:11), signifying peace and deliverance from the flood; a figure of the peace conferred in baptism.
types.displayName: The Dove and the Olive Branch (Noah)

types.name: The Elect (Predestinate)
types.description: Those whom God has chosen and predestined to eternal glory by his mercy, apart from any foreseen merits.

types.name: The Exodus from Egypt
types.description: God's deliverance of Israel from Egyptian bondage; a figure of the redemption of mankind by Christ.

types.name: The Faithful Remnant
types.description: The few of Israel preserved through judgment (e.g. under Hezekiah after the Assyrians); a figure of the remnant who embrace the faith of Christ (Rom 9:27).

types.name: The Feast on Mount Zion
types.description: Isaiah's prophesied banquet of rich food and wine on Mount Zion for all nations; a figure of the Eucharist and the heavenly banquet.

types.name: The Foolish Shepherd
types.description: The foolish/idol shepherd of Zech 11:15, representing the wicked princes and priests (and emperors like Caligula and Nero) who rule before the desolation of Jerusalem.

types.name: The Gates Lifted for the King of Glory
types.description: The eternal gates commanded to lift up their heads for the triumphal entry of the King of Glory (Ps 23/24); a figure of Christ's ascension into heaven.
types.displayName: The Gates Lifted for the King of Glory

types.name: The Gentiles Grafted into Christ's Church
types.displayName: The Gentiles Grafted into Christ's Church

types.name: The Glory of the Lord Departing the Temple
types.description: The divine glory on the throne departing Jerusalem by way of Mount Olivet (Ezek 11:23); read of Christ (two natures on the throne) ascending from Olivet.
types.displayName: The Glory of the Lord Departing the Temple

types.name: The Gospel (New Covenant)
types.description: The Gospel of Jesus Christ, the New Covenant which fulfills and perfects the Law.

types.name: The Heavenly Jerusalem (Prophetic Vision)
types.description: The OT prophetic vision of Jerusalem adorned with precious stones and gold (Tobit 13 / Isaiah 54), prefiguring the glorified Church.

types.name: The Heavens
types.description: The heavens and stars that silently declare God's glory; read as figuring the Church and her apostolic preachers.

types.name: The Holy of Holies
types.description: The innermost sanctuary of the tabernacle/temple, entered once a year by the high priest; a figure of heaven, into which Christ entered by his ascension (Heb 6; 9).

types.name: The Holy Spirit as Divine Guide
types.description: The Holy Spirit who guides the Church and individual believers, as the pillar of cloud guided Israel.
types.displayName: The Holy Spirit as Divine Guide

types.name: The Invitation to the Waters (Isaiah 55)
types.description: Isaiah's invitation to all who thirst to come to the waters, milk, and wine without price; a figure of Christ's invitation and the grace of the sacraments.

types.name: The King of Tyre
types.description: The king of Tyre, 'the seal of resemblance,' whose pride is commonly understood of Lucifer.

types.name: The Kings of Sheba Bearing Gifts
types.description: The kings of Sheba and Ephah prophesied to come bearing gold and frankincense (Isa 60:6); fulfilled in the Magi adoring Christ.
types.displayName: The Kings of Sheba Bearing Gifts

types.name: The Living Waters from the Sanctuary
types.description: The fountain of water flowing from Jerusalem/the temple (Joel 3:18; Ezek 47); a figure of the fountain of grace in the Church militant and of glory in the Church triumphant.
types.displayName: The Living Waters from the Sanctuary

types.name: The Mark of Tau
types.description: The mark Tau (in ancient Hebrew the form of a cross) set on the foreheads of the righteous to spare them (Ezek 9:4); a figure of the sign of Christ's cross in baptism.

types.name: The Mincha (Unbloody Sacrifice)
types.description: The mincha, the unbloody grain/flour offering of the Old Law; a figure of the Mass.

types.name: The Mosaic Law
types.description: The Law (Torah) given to Israel; perfected and fulfilled by the Gospel of Christ (Matt 5:17).

types.name: The Pool of Siloam
types.description: The pool of Siloe ('sent') at Jerusalem; its waters figure the sacrament of baptism, and its name figures Christ the Sent One.

types.name: The Promised Land
types.description: The land of Israel/Judea where right worship was observed; a figure of heaven, 'the land of rectitude.'

types.name: The Prophets
types.description: The Old Testament prophets, who represented God under visible forms and prefigured Christ, the end of the law.

types.name: The Rebuilt Temple
types.description: The second temple, rebuilt under Persian patronage after the exile, enduring despite adversity; a figure of the Church's indestructibility.

types.name: The Rechabites
types.description: The Rechabites who kept strict ascetic rules and abstained from lawful things for greater perfection; a figure of the religious orders of the Church.

types.name: The Rejected Cornerstone
types.description: The stone the builders rejected, become the head of the corner (Ps 117:22); applied to David/Zorobabel/Israel as figures of Christ, rejected then made the foundation.

types.name: The Reprobate (the Rejected)
types.description: Those rejected by God and excluded from salvation, in contrast to the elect.

types.name: The Resurrection
types.description: The resurrection of Christ and the consequent bodily resurrection of believers.

types.name: The Shepherd of Israel
types.description: God/the Messiah portrayed as a shepherd ruling, guiding, and feeding his flock (Ps 23; Ezek 34); fulfilled in Christ the Lamb-Shepherd who leads the saints to fountains of living water.

types.name: The Son of Isaiah (Emmanuel sign)
types.description: The child to be born of Isaiah (Isa 8:4) as a near-term sign of deliverance; a prefigurement of Christ the true Emmanuel.

types.name: The Spouse of the Canticle (Song of Songs)
types.description: The bride/spouse of the Song of Songs, read as the Church seeking and united to Christ the one true Shepherd-Bridegroom.
types.displayName: The Spouse of the Canticle (Song of Songs)

types.name: The Stone (Daniel's Vision)
types.description: The stone cut without hands that shattered the four kingdoms and became a mountain filling the earth (Dan 2); a figure of Christ's eternal kingdom, the Church.

types.name: The Sun
types.description: The sun set in the firmament, giving light and warmth to all the world; read as figuring Christ, the Sun of Justice.

types.name: The Synagogue as Preparation for the Church
types.displayName: The Synagogue as Preparation for the Church

types.name: The Synagogue (Old Covenant Assembly)
types.description: The synagogue/assembly of the Old Covenant which rejected the Messiah; contrasted with the Church that received him as head.

types.name: The Synagogue's Persecution of the Church
types.displayName: The Synagogue's Persecution of the Church

types.name: The Table of Showbread (Bread of the Presence)
types.displayName: The Table of Showbread (Bread of the Presence)

types.name: The Temple of Jerusalem
types.description: The material temple/sanctuary on Zion, stable and singular; fulfilled in the Church and figuring the heavenly dwelling.

types.name: The Threshing Floor
types.description: The threshing floor where grain is separated from chaff by winnowing; a figure of the Church, where the elect are distinguished from the reprobate.

types.name: The Twelve Apostles
types.description: The twelve apostles chosen by Christ, from whom the Christian people descend according to the spirit.

types.name: The Twelve Patriarchs
types.description: The twelve patriarchs, ancestral heads of the tribes of Israel; prefiguring the twelve apostles.

types.name: The Unbroken Bones of the Just
types.description: The bones of the just man that shall not be broken (Ps 33/34:21); fulfilled in Christ, whose bones were not broken (John 19:36).
types.displayName: The Unbroken Bones of the Just

types.name: The Virgin of Emmanuel (Isaiah 7:14)
types.description: The virgin (almah) who shall conceive and bear Emmanuel; fulfilled in the Virgin Mary's conception of Christ.

types.name: The Voice of the Lord (Thunder)
types.description: The sevenfold 'voice of the Lord' (thunder) in Ps 28(29); read of Christ's powerful preaching, his baptism, and the sacraments.

types.name: Wilderness Pilgrimage toward the Promised Land
types.description: Israel's forty-year journey through the wilderness toward the earthly Promised Land.
types.displayName: Wilderness Pilgrimage toward the Promised Land

types.name: The Year of Jubilee
types.description: The Jubilee year (Lev 25) of liberation, debt-forgiveness, and restoration; a figure of Christ's redemption.

types.name: Water from the Rock
types.description: Water that flowed from the rock struck by Moses at Horeb/Meribah to quench Israel's thirst.

types.name: Zechariah's Thirty Pieces of Silver
types.description: The prophet's symbolic action of receiving thirty pieces of silver (the 'handsome price,' ironically) and casting them to the potter in the house of the Lord (Zech 11:12-13); fulfilled in Judas's betrayal.

types.name: Zedekiah
types.description: Sedecias, the last king of Judah, rejected and afflicted; read as figuring Christ rejected and treated thus for the sins of mankind.

types.name: Zorobabel
types.description: The post-exilic leader who, though highly regarded, never truly possessed the throne; a figure of Christ, lest the Jews think the prophecies fulfilled in him.
